svg.title: Figure 5. Gate decision and return map
svg.desc: Evidence, pass, fail, destinations, waiver, and runner-failure handling for G1–G4.
svg.text: A gate checks the evaluation record. A pass means the named evidence is present. It is not a finding that the agent is secure. Stage 7, Stage 9, and Stage 10 are not gates.
Evaluation point: after Stage 2 Threat model. The next stage on a pass is Stage 3 Requirements.

text.tspan: • Stage 2 surface catalog.
• Adversary, goal, and precondition for each in-scope surface,
or an explicit waiver with reason and affected surface.
• Permission levels, or a statement that only one level
exists.
• Memory, peers, and tool code registered or waived. Actuators
registered or recorded as not applicable.
• No runtime trace. Declared test checks are Stage 4, after
this pass, and are not G1 evidence.
Every in-scope surface is named or
explicitly waived.
Destination: Stage 3 Requirements. Stages
3 and 4 are not a second gate.
A surface is neither named nor waived.
Destination: Stage 2 Threat model. Do
not write tests for that surface.
Waiver. The waiver meets the named-or-waived rule for that surface only. It is not a pass and not verification.
Runner failure. Not used at G1.
If evidence is unavailable. A missing adversary, goal, precondition, or waiver fails G1 and returns to Stage 2.

svg.text: Evaluation point: after Stage 5 Run. The next stage on a pass is Stage 6 Score.

text.tspan: • Ordered trace for each scored case, linked to the run
manifest.
• Case, requirement, pair, and role. Agent and model version.
Tool-registry version.
• Tool name, arguments, result, committed flag. Sequence
number. Timestamp if stored.
• Memory, peer, or actuator events only when that component is
registered.
• Integrity, completeness, provenance, and timestamp
consistency all hold.
The trace passes those checks. A raw log
that fails them is not scoring evidence.
Destination: Stage 6 Score.
Any of the four checks fails, or a tool
log is missing.
Destination: Stage 5 Run. Do not invent
the missing call from the model’s
sentence.
Waiver. Waived surfaces add no events. That absence is not a G2 failure and is not verification.
Runner failure. No trace was produced. Log it apart and stop. Not a G2 pass. Not a defense success. Not a security finding. Outside every
denominator. No retry count is defined.
If evidence is unavailable. If those fields cannot be logged, G2 fails and the run is not reported as an evaluation.

svg.text: Evaluation point: after Stage 6 Score. The next stage on a pass is Stage 7 Detect. G3 does not check DC, FN, or FP.

text.tspan: • Carrier the system actually reads. A payload pasted only
into the system prompt fails this gate.
• Stage 4 predicate over trace fields, and the observed
outcome of that predicate.
• TS, AS, UA, and CS, each recomputed with its protocol
numerator and denominator.
• The same pairs for task success and attack success.
• Not detection timing. Stage 7 assigns pre-commit,
post-commit, missed, and not monitored after the pass.
The Stage 6 numbers recompute from the
predicates and the trace fields.
Destination: Stage 7 Detect.
Wrong check or carrier
Stage 4 Tests. Includes a payload
pasted only into the system prompt.
Arithmetic only
Stage 6 Score. The predicate and the
carrier stay as declared.
System change
Stage 2 Threat model. Model, tool
registry, memory policy, peer set,
or actuator set. Not the G1 failure.
Do not attribute it to the control.
Waiver. A waiver is not a G3 pass. An empty metric cell is not a waived pass.
Runner failure. Does not reach G3. Excluded at G2.
If evidence is unavailable. A predicate or field that cannot be recomputed fails the gate. Carrier or predicate: Stage 4. Arithmetic: Stage 6. A
changed system returns to Stage 2, as its own path.

svg.text: Evaluation point: after Stage 8 Mitigate. The next stage on a pass is Stage 9 Recover.

text.tspan: • Named controls with class and observation point.
• Same pairs, rerun, with new protected-run traces.
• Baseline TS and protected TS, each with its own |B|.
• Leftover requirement identifiers. Identifiers, not a bare
count.
• Changed-attack DC and FP on the second manifest, plus
unmonitored identifiers, or an explicit waiver.
• Recovery-rerun task success is Stage 9. It is not a G4
column.
Controls, rerun, both TS columns,
leftovers, and a changed-attack rerun or a
written waiver.
Destination: Stage 9 Recover. Lower AS
alone does not pass. A pass does not clear
a security finding.
Any required item is missing, or the
first manifest’s DC or FP is copied into
a waived CAC cell.
Destination: Stage 8 Mitigate.
Waiver. A CAC waiver may fill that cell. It is not a pass, not verification, and not the first manifest’s rates. The other evidence is still
required.
Runner failure. On a rerun, the same separate record as G2. Not defense success. Not in the protected denominators.
If evidence is unavailable. No rerun and no waiver, or no leftover identifiers: unfinished. Return to Stage 8.

svg.text: A held attack check or a leftover identifier is a security finding, not a gate failure. A gate pass does not repair it. Stage 9 lists an irreversible residual and does not call that residual a successful recovery.
